**A dialog can be answered without the screen, and the terminal survives it**

investigation · 2026-09-09

the finding it corrects: [MUS-F-0113](../findings.md#mus-f-0113)

the correction: [MUS-F-0120](../findings.md#mus-f-0120)

the question it informs: [MUS-Q-0085](../questions.md#mus-q-0085)

## Context

Run because MUS-F-0113 was read rather than measured, and everything the proposed session-channel milestone gains over MUS-D-0143 turned on one unmeasured behaviour.

It can be done. It cannot be done through the event the finding named, which is MUS-F-0120.

Two limits are recorded so nobody reads more into the verdict than it says. The picker half of the pane parser stays: nothing here touched the model picker, the effort cycler or the toggles of MUS-F-0101, which are drawn on the owner's own keypress and fire no hook. And the workspace-trust prompt is drawn before the session exists, so it is one dialog no hook can reach -- not in the rule's way, since a session started in a directory the owner has already trusted never sees it, but a module that assumes every dialog is interceptable would hang on the first one of a session's life.

Route C was not touched, which is what ordering the routes was for. Route B was not re-run, as pre-registered; the one fact re-checked is unchanged, and at 2.1.266 the streaming flags are still marked as working only with --print.

Written up in docs/investigations/0003-dialog-without-the-screen.md, with the harness and the captured payloads beside it.

## Rule

Three properties, all required -- interceptable, answerable, terminal-preserving -- holding on five consecutive trials of the same shape with no trial reading a pane. One failure in five fails the route. Property 3 checked after every trial rather than once. Timeout measured separately over three trials and not pass/fail. Committed at 0bf164b, before any evidence was looked at.

## Result

Route A passes. Seven firings carried tool_name, tool_input and permission_suggestions that are the drawn dialog's own options. allow ran the tool and drew no dialog; deny stopped it and its reason reached the agent verbatim. A second client attached over its own tmux socket rendered the conversation and typed into it, on all five. Three hold trials all ended with the CLI waiting out the hook and drawing its own dialog -- 21.3s, 24s and 20s at a 20s hook timeout -- so the fallback is the parser that already exists.

## Verified against

Claude Code 2.1.263 for the five trials and 2.1.266 for the confirmation; the CLI updated itself mid-run and both versions are named rather than one being claimed for the other.
